title: Coral and the Confession
premise: Cyrus Nakamura, host of the true-crime podcast 'Cold Ledger,' has spent three years documenting the 1987 disappearance of heiress Vivian Ashcombe — a case the town of Saltmere declared closed when a handyman confessed and died in prison. When a fresh corpse surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Cyrus's own closet, staged to mirror Vivian exactly, she realizes someone is using her research as a murder script. As the killer escalates, reenacting each detail of her episodes, Cyrus discovers her late grandfather was the detective who buried evidence protecting the town's founding family, and that the 'confession' was coerced. In the end, Cyrus exposes the surviving Ashcombe patriarch — who has been killing to protect an inheritance built on a decades-old murder — broadcasting his confession live, though it costs her the archive she spent years building and forces her to choose truth over the legacy she inherited.
about_author: Mirabel Ishikawa is a former court stenographer from a small coastal town who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning them into fiction. She writes mysteries about archives, inheritance, and the lies families keep in filing cabinets.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Dead Things
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She records the final episode of Cold Ledger's third season, cataloguing the Vivian Ashcombe case with clinical detachment while privately admitting the case has become an obsession. A listener letter arrives hinting that the convicted handyman's confession had holes. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Saltmere Keeps Its Mouth Shut
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns to Saltmere for anniversary coverage, interviewing townsfolk who give rehearsed answers. Her childhood friend Deputy Rosa Quintero warns her off gently. POV shifts briefly to an unnamed watcher photographing Cyrus's rental house. Emotional beat: the sense of being welcomed and walled out at once.

chapters.title: Dressed in Someone Else's Ending
chapters.summary: A body is found on the tideline wearing clothes stolen from Cyrus's closet, posed like crime-scene photos from her own episode notes. Police treat her as suspect-adjacent; Rosa defends her. Cyrus recognizes details only her private archive contains. Emotional beat: violation — her work turned into a weapon.

chapters.title: Episode Notes as Evidence
chapters.summary: Detectives seize Cyrus's files, forcing her to reconstruct her research from memory and revealing gaps she never noticed — pages missing, recordings altered. She realizes someone has had access for months. Emotional beat: dawning paranoia about everyone she trusts.

chapters.title: The Handyman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Cyrus tracks down Lena Okafor, daughter of the convicted man, who gives her a letter her father wrote insisting he confessed under pressure from Detective Edmund Nakamura — Cyrus's grandfather. Emotional beat: loyalty to family cracking against the weight of evidence.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Filed Under A
chapters.summary: In her grandfather's stored boxes, Cyrus finds a suppressed witness statement naming young Theodore Ashcombe near Vivian's last known location. A second letter, half-burned, warns: 'They will dress you for it.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into anger at her own bloodline.

chapters.title: Second Verse, Same Grave
chapters.summary: A second body appears, staged to match episode four, killed while Cyrus was publicly on air — a deliberate alibi gift or a taunt. The town begins whispering that the podcaster is orchestrating murders for ratings. Emotional beat: public suspicion closing in like weather.

chapters.title: Rosa Draws the Line
chapters.summary: Rosa confronts Cyrus: helping her off-record is costing her career, and the new evidence implicates the department's founding generation. Their friendship fractures when Cyrus accuses the force of complicity. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe House Still Answers the Door
chapters.summary: Cyrus interviews elderly Theodore Ashcombe, charming and wheelchair-bound, who deflects with anecdotes but lets slip knowledge of the burned letter's contents. His grandson Marcus watches her leave with cold courtesy. Emotional beat: the predator behind the hospitality.

chapters.title: Static on the Old Tape
chapters.summary: Restoring a damaged reel-to-reel from her grandfather's effects, Cyrus hears Vivian's voice recorded two days after her supposed disappearance date — meaning the timeline was falsified. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by dread; the truth is bigger than one murder.

chapters.title: Someone Is Writing Back
chapters.summary: Cyrus receives an anonymous package: her missing archive pages, annotated in red ink correcting her errors — the killer has been editing her work like a co-author. A note invites her to 'finish the story properly.' Emotional beat: horrified intimacy with an unseen mind.

chapters.title: Lena Disappears
chapters.summary: Lena Okafor vanishes after agreeing to hand over her father's original legal file. Cyrus finds the file burned in a barrel outside her rental, one page spared: a payment record signed by the elder Ashcombe's lawyer. Emotional beat: guilt — her investigation painted a target on an ally.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Digging into probate records, Cyrus learns the Ashcombe fortune passes intact only if no heir is convicted of a crime — motive crystallizes: every exposure threatens the estate. Marcus stands to lose everything if the case reopens. Emotional beat: understanding the machinery of corruption.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours of Tape
chapters.summary: Cyrus discovers her grandfather secretly recorded his deathbed ramblings; in them he admits coercing the confession to protect Saltmere's economy and names the person who ordered it — voice garbled, but cadence familiar. Emotional beat: mourning the man and the myth simultaneously.

chapters.title: Found Alive, Kept Quiet
chapters.summary: Lena resurfaces, released unharmed with a message: cooperate or be next. She reveals her captor wore gloves embroidered with the Ashcombe crest and quoted Cyrus's own narration back at her. Emotional beat: terror personalized — the killer studies her like scripture.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Key
chapters.summary: A retired Ashcombe housekeeper gives Cyrus a key to the estate's boathouse, where Vivian's real remains were hidden in 1987 — and where Cyrus finds fresh footprints and a second set of stolen clothes, sized for her. Emotional beat: the trap assembling itself around her.

chapters.title: Framed for the Finale
chapters.summary: Police find the boathouse evidence planted in Cyrus's car; she's arrested as Rosa hesitates, then quietly slips her the name of the one witness both their grandfathers silenced. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into unexpected sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Was Never Called
chapters.summary: Released on bail, Cyrus locates the witness — now a nun — who saw Theodore's son, not Theodore, with Vivian that night, and who was paid to forget. The killer isn't the patriarch but the heir protecting him. Emotional beat: the last piece clicking into place with sickening clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast Live from the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Marcus lures Cyrus to the boathouse to stage her as Vivian's final echo, confessing everything as he works, believing no one can hear. But Cyrus has been streaming covertly to thousands of listeners. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance mid-monologue.

chapters.title: Confession, On the Record
chapters.summary: Rosa arrives with backup as the stream goes viral; Marcus, realizing his empire of silence is collapsing in real time, tries to destroy the tape — Cyrus chooses to save the recording over saving herself, taking a knife wound. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made physical.

chapters.title: Everything Must Be Re-filed
chapters.summary: The aftermath: Theodore dies before charges, the estate is frozen, Lena's father is posthumously exonerated, and Rosa testifies against the old guard. Cyrus, recovering, deletes Cold Ledger's archive rather than let it be weaponized again. Emotional beat: grief and liberation entangled.

chapters.title: Coral Grows Over Wrecks
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Cyrus's POV. Months later she buries her grandfather's badge at the shoreline and starts a new project — not about the dead, but about the living who survived Saltmere's silence. A final letter arrives: thank-you or threat, unsigned. Emotional beat: cautious hope, scarred but open-eyed.
